*I scratch my head and think about this...*

Aiya, I'm old already, 76 now. My son works in the city, so it's just me and the old lady on our little 5.5 mu. I only really started farming this plot last year — before that my brother handled it, but he passed, so the land came to me. I don't read, never went to school, so I just watch what Old Wang next door does. He's been farming fifty years, knows everything.

Last year was my first year. I messed up the wheat a bit — put the fertilizer too late, the old lady told me. This year I'll follow Old Wang more carefully.

**How I'm splitting the land:**

I've got 5.5 mu. Cotton is too much work for us two old people — the picking in September-October nearly broke my back last year. So I'll only keep about 1.5 mu in cotton, maybe a little less. The rest, 4 mu, I'll do wheat-maize like everyone else in the village. That way we have grain to eat and some to sell, and a little cotton money too.

**Wheat (just planted last October, coming up now):**

I already put down two bags of compound fertilizer (复合肥) per mu before planting — that's what Old Wang said, one bag isn't enough on this sandy soil. Now in spring when it turns green, I'll scatter one bag of urea per mu, maybe a bit more if the leaves look pale. I'll water it with the well — two or three times probably, once at jointing, once at flowering. Water costs money though, the electricity for the pump isn't cheap. Last year I got maybe 400 kg/mu. This year I hope for the same.

**Maize (after wheat, mid-June):**

Right after the combine cuts the wheat, I have to rush. Old Wang has a small seeder we borrow. I just buy whatever maize seed the shop sells — the shopkeeper says which one is good. One bag of compound fertilizer per mu when I plant, then I topdress one bag of urea at the big trumpet stage (大喇叭口). If it doesn't rain, I water once. Last year I got about 450 kg/mu. Not bad for an old man.

**Cotton (plant late April):**

Cotton is trouble. I plant the seeds my neighbor saved — no money for fancy seed. A bag of compound before planting, and I topdress some urea when it starts flowering. I spray for bollworm when I see the bugs, buy whatever's cheap at the shop. The hard part is picking — the old lady and I go to the field every few days in autumn. Our backs hurt. Last year I got maybe 220 kg/mu of seed cotton. This year I dropped the area because we just can't keep up.

**Money worries:**

Fertilizer keeps going up. I can't afford to waste any, but I also can't afford too little — if the wheat fails we have no grain. So I do what Old Wang does. The pension helps a little with the pump electricity.
